title.zh: 卷四九 補列傳第四一 方伎
title.raw: 卷四九 補列傳第四一 方伎 Volume 49 Biographies 41: Arts

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：定天下之吉兇，成天下之亹亹，莫善於蓍龜。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: To settle the auspice and bane of the realm and to accomplish the realm’s tireless striving, nothing is better than milfoil and tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: To discern fortune and ruin for the realm and to sustain its ceaseless work, nothing surpasses divination by milfoil and tortoise.

sentences.zh: 是故天生神物，聖人則之。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven produces numinous things, and the sage takes them as his model.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven produces sacred things, and the sage models himself upon them.

sentences.zh: 又神農、桐君論《本草》藥性，黃帝、岐伯說病候治方，皆聖人之所重也。

translations.literal: Again, Shennong and Lord Tong discussed the properties of drugs in the Root Canon of Materia Medica; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo explained symptoms and healing prescriptions—all were prized by sages.
translations.idiomatic: Shennong and Lord Tong classified herbs in the Root Canon; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo set forth disease and cure—all arts the sages held dear.

sentences.zh: 故太史公著《龜策》、《日者》及《扁鵲倉公傳》，皆所以廣其聞見，昭示後昆。

translations.literal: Thus Grand Historian Sima Qian wrote the “Treatises on Tortoises and Divination,” “The Day Diviners,” and the “Biographies of Bian Que and Lord Cang”—all to broaden knowledge and show the way to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Sima Qian’s treatises on tortoise divination, day-selection, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang—all to widen what we know and guide posterity.

sentences.zh: 齊氏作霸以來，招引英俊，但有藝能，無不畢策，今並錄之以備《方伎》云。

translations.literal: Since Qi rose to hegemony, it has recruited outstanding men; whoever had any skill was exhaustively enlisted. Now all are recorded here to complete the “Arts and Techniques.”
translations.idiomatic: Since Qi began its rise, it has gathered talent; anyone with a craft was pressed into service. They are recorded here for the account of Arts and Techniques.

sentences.zh: 由吾道榮 王春 信都芳 宋景業 許遵 吳遵世 趙輔和 皇甫玉 解法選 魏寧 綦母懷文 張子信 馬嗣明

translations.literal: You Wudao Rong, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimu Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, Ma Siming
translations.idiomatic: You Wudao Rong, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimu Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, and Ma Siming

sentences.zh: 由吾道榮，琅邪人。

translations.literal: You Wudao Rong was a native of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: You Wudao Rong was from Langye.

sentences.zh: 少好道法，與其同類相求，入長白、太山潛隱，具聞道術。

translations.literal: In youth he loved the Way and its methods; with like-minded companions he sought one another, entered Mount Changbai and Mount Tai to live in seclusion, and heard the full range of Daoist arts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved Daoist practice; with kindred spirits he withdrew to Mount Changbai and Mount Tai and mastered the arts of the Way.

sentences.zh: 仍遊鄒、魯之間，習儒業。

translations.literal: He then traveled between Zou and Lu and studied Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: He later wandered between Zou and Lu and studied the classics.

sentences.zh: 晉陽人某，大明法術，乃尋之。

translations.literal: A certain man of Jinyang, greatly skilled in the arts, therefore went in search of him.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Jinyang, deeply versed in the arts, set out to find him.

sentences.zh: 是人為人家庸力，無識之者，久乃訪知。

translations.literal: This man was hired labor in someone’s household; no one knew who he was, and only after a long search was he found out.
translations.idiomatic: The man was a hired hand in a private home; none knew his worth until a long search revealed him.

sentences.zh: 其人道家符水、咒禁、陰陽歷數、天文、藥性無不通解，以道榮好尚，乃悉授之。

translations.literal: The man was thoroughly versed in Daoist talismanic water, incantatory prohibitions, yin-yang calendrics, astronomy, and pharmacology; because Dao Rong admired these things, he taught him everything.
translations.idiomatic: He knew talismans, spells, calendrics, astronomy, and medicine; seeing Dao Rong’s devotion, he taught him all of it.

sentences.zh: 是人謂道榮雲：「我本恒岳仙人，有少罪過，為天官所謫。

translations.literal: The man said to Dao Rong, “I am originally an immortal of Mount Heng; for a small offense I was demoted by the celestial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The man told Dao Rong, “I am an immortal of Mount Heng, banished for a minor fault by heaven’s officers.

sentences.zh: 今限滿將歸，卿宜送吾至汾水。

translations.literal: My term is now ending and I am about to return; you should escort me to the Fen River.”
translations.idiomatic: My term is up and I must return—escort me to the Fen.”

sentences.zh: 」及河，值水暴長，橋壞，船渡艱難。

translations.literal: When they reached the river, the water had swollen violently, the bridge was broken, and crossing by boat was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At the river the flood had burst its banks, the bridge was gone, and boats could scarcely cross.

sentences.zh: 是人乃臨水禹步，以一符投水中，流便絕。

translations.literal: The man then performed Yu’s paces beside the water and cast a talisman into the stream; the current stopped at once.
translations.idiomatic: He paced the Yu steps at the bank and threw a talisman into the water; the current halted.

sentences.zh: 俄頃水積將至天，是人徐自沙石上渡。

translations.literal: In a moment the piled water rose nearly to the sky; the man slowly crossed over on the sand and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Water piled to the sky; he walked calmly across on the stones of the ford.

sentences.zh: 唯道榮見其如是，傍人咸云水如此長，此人遂能浮過，共驚異之。

translations.literal: Only Dao Rong saw him do this; bystanders all said that with water so high this man could still float across, and together they marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dao Rong saw how it was done; onlookers, seeing him cross such a flood, were astounded.

sentences.zh: 道榮仍歸本部，隱於琅邪山，辟穀，餌松術、茯苓，求長生之秘。

translations.literal: Dao Rong returned to his home region, hid on Mount Langye, abstained from grain, ate pine shoots and tuckahoe, and sought the secret of long life.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Rong went home to Mount Langye, lived on pine and tuckahoe, abstained from grain, and sought immortality.

sentences.zh: 尋為顯祖追往晉陽。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned by Emperor Xianzu to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianzu summoned him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 至遼陽山中，有猛獸去馬十步，所追人驚怖將走。

translations.literal: In the mountains of Liaoyang a fierce beast stood ten paces from the horses; those in pursuit were terrified and about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaoyang hills a beast blocked the road ten paces from the horses; the escort panicked and nearly fled.

sentences.zh: 道榮以杖畫地成火坑，猛獸遽走。

translations.literal: Dao Rong drew a fire pit on the ground with his staff, and the beast fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Rong traced a fiery pit with his staff, and the beast bolted.

sentences.zh: 俄值國廢，道榮歸周。

translations.literal: Soon the state was abolished, and Dao Rong went over to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Dao Rong entered Zhou service.

sentences.zh: 隋初乃卒。

translations.literal: In the early Sui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in early Sui times.

sentences.zh: 又有張遠遊者，顯祖時令與諸術士合九轉金丹。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Yuanyou; in Xianzu’s time he was ordered to compound the nine-times-transmuted golden elixir with other masters of the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanyou, in Xianzu’s day, was set to refine the ninefold golden elixir with other adepts.

sentences.zh: 及成，顯祖置之玉匣，云：「我貪世間作樂，不能卽飛上天，待臨死時取服。」

translations.literal: When it was finished, Xianzu placed it in a jade casket and said, “I am greedy for the pleasures of the world and cannot at once fly up to Heaven; I shall take it when I am about to die.”
translations.idiomatic: When the elixir was ready, Xianzu locked it in a jade box: “I love the world too well to ascend now—I will swallow it on my deathbed.”

sentences.zh: 王春，河東人，少好易占，明風角，遊於趙、魏之間，飛符上天。

translations.literal: Wang Chun was a native of Hedong; in youth he loved Changes divination, understood wind angles, traveled between Zhao and Wei, and sent talismans flying to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chun of Hedong loved the Changes in youth, read the winds, wandered Zhao and Wei, and was famed for sending talismans heavenward.

sentences.zh: 高祖起於信都，引為館客。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose at Xindu, Chun was brought in as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner at Xindu, Chun became his house diviner.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之戰，四面受敵，從寅至午，三合三離。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling they were attacked on all sides; from the yin hour to the wu hour they joined battle three times and broke off three times.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling they were surrounded; from dawn to noon they clashed three times and broke off three times.

sentences.zh: 高祖將退軍，春叩馬諫曰：「比未時，必當大捷。

translations.literal: Gaozu was about to withdraw; Chun seized his horse’s bridle and remonstrated, “By the wei hour there will certainly be a great victory.”
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu meant to retreat; Chun caught his bridle: “Before mid-afternoon you will win decisively.”

sentences.zh: 」遽縛其子詣王為質，不勝請斬之。

translations.literal: He immediately bound his son and brought him to the prince as a hostage, begging that if he was wrong his son be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He bound his son and offered him as hostage, asking to be beheaded himself if he proved wrong.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊大敗。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 其後每從征討，其言多中，位徐州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Thereafter on every campaign his words mostly hit true; he rose to Inspector of Xu Province and died.
translations.idiomatic: On later campaigns his forecasts usually proved right; he became inspector of Xu Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 信都芳，河間人。

translations.literal: Xindu Fang was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu Fang was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少明算術，為州裏所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in calculation and was praised in his district.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at mathematics and was praised locally.

sentences.zh: 有巧思，每精研究，忘寢與食，或墜坑坎。

translations.literal: He had ingenious thought; whenever he studied closely he forgot sleep and food and sometimes fell into pits and ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Ingenious and obsessive, he forgot food and sleep over his work and once fell into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人云：「算之妙，機巧精微，我每一沈思，不聞雷霆之聲也。

translations.literal: He once told someone, “The subtlety of calculation—its ingenuity and fineness—whenever I ponder deeply I do not hear the sound of thunder.”
translations.idiomatic: He said, “Calculation is so subtle that when I ponder it I hear no thunder.”

sentences.zh: 」其用心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the concentration of his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his concentration.

sentences.zh: 以術數干高祖為館客，授參軍丞相倉曹。

translations.literal: By numerology he sought Gaozu and became a house guest, appointed Staff Officer in the Chancellor’s Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his arts to Gaozu, became a house guest, and was made staff officer in the chancellor’s granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 祖珽謂芳曰：「律管吹灰，術甚微妙，絕來旣久，吾思所不至，卿試思之。

translations.literal: Zu Ting said to Fang, “Blowing ash through pitch-pipes is an extremely subtle art long lost; I cannot think it through—try to work it out.”
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting said, “The pitch-pipe ash test is subtle and long lost—I cannot recover it; try.”

sentences.zh: 」芳遂留意，十數日，便云：「吾得矣，然終須河內葭莩灰。

translations.literal: Fang then applied himself; in a dozen days he said, “I have it—but in the end we need reed-ash from Henei.”
translations.idiomatic: Fang labored ten days and said, “I have it—but only with reed-ash from Henei.”

sentences.zh: 」後得河內葭莩，用其術，應節便飛，餘灰卽不動也。

translations.literal: Later they obtained Henei reed-ash; using his method, at the proper season it flew, while other ashes did not move.
translations.idiomatic: With Henei reed-ash the ash leapt at each season’s turn; other ash stayed still.

sentences.zh: 不為時所重，竟不行，故此法遂絕云。

translations.literal: He was not valued by his time and the method was never put into practice, so the art died out.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored him, the method was never used, and the art died out.

sentences.zh: 芳又撰次古來渾天、地動、欹器、漏刻諸巧事，並畫圖，名曰《器準》。

translations.literal: Fang also compiled ancient ingenious devices—the armillary sphere, earthquake indicator, tipping vessel, and clepsydra—illustrated them, and titled the work Standards of Instruments.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ancient devices—armillary spheres, seismoscopes, tipping vessels, clepsydras—illustrated them in Standards of Instruments.

sentences.zh: 又著《樂書》、《遁甲經》、《四術周髀宗》。

translations.literal: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and the Four Arts and Gnomon of the Zhou Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and Four Arts and the Gnomon of the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 芳又私撰歷書，名為《靈憲歷》，算月有頻大頻小，食必以朔，證據甚甄明，每云：「何承天亦為此法，不能精，靈憲若成，必當百代無異議。

translations.literal: Fang also privately drafted a calendar called the Spiritual Constitution Calendar, calculating that the moon is sometimes large and sometimes small and that eclipses must fall on new moon; the evidence was very clear. He often said, “He Chengtian also used this method but could not refine it; if the Spiritual Constitution is completed, for a hundred generations there will be no dispute.”
translations.idiomatic: His private Spiritual Constitution Calendar tracked the moon’s varying size and fixed eclipses at new moon with rare clarity. “He Chengtian tried this but lacked precision,” he said; “finish this calendar and posterity will not quarrel.”

sentences.zh: 」書未就而卒。

translations.literal: The book was unfinished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the book was finished.

sentences.zh: 宋景業，廣宗人。

translations.literal: Song Jingye was a native of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingye was from Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 明《周易》，為陰陽，緯候之學，兼明歷數。

translations.literal: He understood the Book of Changes, practiced yin-yang and weft-text prognostication, and was also skilled in calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Changes, yin-yang lore, weft-text prophecy, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 魏末，任北平守。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he served as Administrator of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei he governed Beiping.

sentences.zh: 顯祖作相，在晉陽，景業因高德政上言：「《易稽覽圖》曰：『《鼎》，五月，聖人君，天與延年齒，東北水中，庶人王，高得之。

translations.literal: When Xianzu was chief minister at Jinyang, Jingye through Gao Dezheng submitted: “The Changes Appraisal Diagram says: ‘The Hexagram Ding, in the fifth month—a sage rules; Heaven grants extended years; in the northeastern waters a common man becomes king; Gao obtains it.’”
translations.idiomatic: While Xianzu was chief minister at Jinyang, Jingye reported through Gao Dezheng: “The Appraisal Diagram of the Changes reads: ‘Ding, the fifth month—a sage reigns; Heaven grants long life; in the northeastern waters a commoner becomes king; Gao shall obtain it.’”

sentences.zh: 』謹案東北水謂渤海也，高得之，明高氏得天下也。

translations.literal: “Examining the text, the northeastern waters mean Bohai; Gao obtains it—this shows the Gao clan will gain the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: “The northeastern waters are Bohai; ‘Gao obtains it’ means the Gao will take the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」是時魏武定八年五月也。

translations.literal: It was then the fifth month of the eighth year of Wuding in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifth month of Wei Wuding year eight.

sentences.zh: 高德政、徐之才並勸顯祖應天受禪，乃之鄴。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai both urged Xianzu to accept Heaven’s mandate; he then went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai urged Xianzu to take the throne, and he marched on Ye.

sentences.zh: 至平城都，諸大臣沮計，將還。

translations.literal: When he reached Pingcheng capital, the great ministers discouraged the plan and he was about to return.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingcheng the ministers dissuaded him and he nearly turned back.

sentences.zh: 賀拔仁等又云：「景業誤王，宜斬之以謝天下。

translations.literal: Heba Ren and others also said, “Jingye has misled the prince; he should be beheaded to appease the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: Heba Ren urged, “Jingye misled you—behead him to satisfy the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」顯祖曰：「景業當為帝王師，何可殺也。

translations.literal: Xianzu said, “Jingye will be the emperor’s teacher—how can he be killed?”
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu said, “Jingye is fit to teach emperors—he cannot be killed.”

sentences.zh: 」還至幷，顯祖令景業筮，遇《乾》之《鼎》。

translations.literal: Returning to Bing, Xianzu ordered Jingye to divine and obtained Qian changing to Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Bing, Xianzu had Jingye cast the hexagrams and drew Qian changing to Ding.

sentences.zh: 景業曰：「《乾》為君，天也。

translations.literal: Jingye said, “Qian is the ruler—Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: Jingye said, “Qian is the ruler—it is Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『時乘六龍以禦天。

translations.literal: The Changes says: “In season he rides the six dragons to govern Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, “He rides six dragons to govern Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 』《鼎》，五月卦也。

translations.literal: “Ding is the hexagram of the fifth month.”
translations.idiomatic: “Ding is the fifth-month hexagram.”

sentences.zh: 宜以仲夏吉辰御天受禪。

translations.literal: You should on an auspicious day in midsummer mount Heaven and receive the abdication.”
translations.idiomatic: Take the throne on an auspicious midsummer day.”

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「陰陽書，五月不可入官，犯之卒於其位。

translations.literal: Someone said, “In books of yin-yang, the fifth month is forbidden for entering office; to violate it is to die in one’s post.”
translations.idiomatic: Others cited yin-yang taboos: “The fifth month forbids taking office—violators die in their posts.”

sentences.zh: 」景業曰：「此乃大吉，王為天子，無復下期，豈得不終於其位。

translations.literal: Jingye said, “This is in fact great good fortune: when the prince becomes Son of Heaven there is no next term—how could he not end in his post?”
translations.idiomatic: Jingye answered, “That is excellent: as Son of Heaven you have no term to end—how would you not die in office?”

sentences.zh: 」顯祖大悅。

translations.literal: Xianzu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 天保初，授散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was made gentleman attendant at the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又有荊次德，有術數，預知尒朱榮成敗，又言代魏者齊。

translations.literal: There was also Jing Cide, skilled in numerology, who foretold the success or failure of Erzhu Rong and also said that Qi would replace Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Cide, versed in numerology, foretold Erzhu Rong’s fall and declared that Qi would replace Wei.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，故自號齊王。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong heard this, he therefore styled himself King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong heard this and took the title King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 待次德以殊禮，問其天人之事。

translations.literal: He treated Cide with exceptional courtesy and asked him about affairs of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong honored him and asked about heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「齊當興，東海出天子，今王據渤海，是齊地。

translations.literal: He replied, “Qi is about to rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. Your Majesty now holds Bohai—that is Qi territory.”
translations.idiomatic: Cide answered, “Qi will rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. You hold Bohai—that is Qi’s ground.”

sentences.zh: 又太白與月幷，宜速用兵，遲則不吉。

translations.literal: “Moreover Venus and the moon are together; you should use troops quickly—delay is unlucky.”
translations.idiomatic: “Venus stands with the moon—strike at once; delay is ill-omened.”

sentences.zh: 」榮不從也。

translations.literal: Rong did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Rong ignored him.

sentences.zh: 許遵，高陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Zun was a native of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zun was from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 明《易》，善筮，兼曉天文、風角、占相、逆刺，其驗若神。

translations.literal: He understood the Changes, was skilled at milfoil divination, and also knew astronomy, wind angles, physiognomy, and reverse needle techniques; his verification was like a spirit’s.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Changes and milfoil, astronomy, wind lore, physiognomy, and geomantic needles—with uncanny accuracy.

sentences.zh: 高祖引為館客，自言祿命不富貴，不橫死，是以任性疏誕，多所犯忤，高祖常容惜之。

translations.literal: Gaozu brought him in as a house guest; Zun said himself that his allotted fate was not wealth and nobility and that he would not die a violent death, and therefore he was willful, unrestrained, and often offensive, yet Gaozu always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu kept him as house diviner; Zun said his fate held neither riches nor violent death, so he spoke freely and often gave offense, yet Gaozu indulged him.

sentences.zh: 邙陰之役，遵謂李業興曰：「彼為火陣，我木陣，火勝木，我必敗。

translations.literal: In the campaign on the north bank of the Mang, Zun said to Li Yexing, “They have a fire formation and we a wood formation; fire overcomes wood—we are certain to lose.”
translations.idiomatic: At the Mang’s north bank he told Li Yexing, “Their formation is fire, ours wood—fire defeats wood; we will lose.”

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: It turned out exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It happened as he said.

sentences.zh: 清河王岳以遵為開府田曹記室。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue appointed Zun recorder in the opening staff’s field bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Yue made him recorder in his field bureau.

sentences.zh: 岳封王，以告遵，遵曰：「蜜蜂亦作王。

translations.literal: When Yue was enfeoffed prince, he told Zun; Zun said, “Bees also make kings.”
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became a prince, Zun remarked, “Bees make kings too.”

sentences.zh: 」岳後將救江陵，遵曰：「此行必致後凶，宜辭疾勿去。

translations.literal: Later, when Yue was about to march to relieve Jiangling, Zun said, “This expedition will bring later calamity; you should plead illness and not go.”
translations.idiomatic: When Yue prepared to relieve Jiangling, Zun warned, “This march brings disaster—plead illness and stay.”

sentences.zh: 」岳曰：「勢不免去，正當與君同行。

translations.literal: Yue said, “I cannot avoid going; I should go with you.”
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, “I cannot refuse—I ought to take you along.”

sentences.zh: 」遵曰：「好與生人相隨，不欲共死人同路。

translations.literal: Zun said, “I like to keep company with the living and do not wish to travel the same road as the dead.”
translations.idiomatic: Zun said, “I keep company with the living—I will not share a road with the dead.”

translations.literal: He returned.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 岳至京尋喪。

translations.literal: Yue reached the capital and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reached the capital and soon died.

sentences.zh: 顯祖無道日甚，遵語人曰：「多折算來，吾筮此狂夫何時當死。

translations.literal: As Xianzu’s lawlessness grew daily, Zun told people, “I have calculated repeatedly when this madman will die.”
translations.idiomatic: As Xianzu grew more lawless, Zun said, “I keep casting when this madman will die.”

sentences.zh: 」遂布算滿床，大言曰：「不出冬初，我乃不見。

translations.literal: He spread counting-rods over the bed and declared loudly, “Before the beginning of winter I shall not see him.”
translations.idiomatic: He spread rods across his bed and cried, “Before winter I shall not see him.”

sentences.zh: 」顯祖以十月崩，遵果以九月死。

translations.literal: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun indeed died in the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun died in the ninth as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 吳遵世，字季緒，渤海人，少學《易》，入恒山從隱居道士遊處。

translations.literal: Wu Zunshi, courtesy name Jixu, was a native of Bohai; in youth he studied the Changes and entered Mount Heng to wander with a reclusive Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zunshi, styled Jixu, was from Bohai; he studied the Changes in youth and lived with a hermit priest on Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 數年，忽見一老翁謂之云：「授君開心符。

translations.literal: After several years an old man suddenly said to him, “I give you the talisman that opens the heart.”
translations.idiomatic: After years an old man said, “I give you the Heart-Opening Talisman.”

sentences.zh: 」遵世跪取吞之，遂明占候。

translations.literal: Zunshi knelt, took it, and swallowed it; thereafter he was clear in prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi knelt, swallowed it, and became a master of divination.

sentences.zh: 後出遊京洛，以《易》筮知名。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to the capital region and became famous for Changes divination.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he became famed for the Changes.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝之將卽位也，使遵世筮之，遇《明夷》之《賁》曰：「初登于天，後入于地。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was about to ascend the throne, he had Zunshi divine and obtained Mingyi changing to Bi, saying, “First he ascends to Heaven, afterward he enters the earth.”
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei Wudi took the throne, Zunshi cast Mingyi changing to Bi: “First he rises to heaven, then he goes into the earth.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: The emperor said, “What does that mean?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “What does that mean?”

sentences.zh: 」遵世曰：「初登于天，當作天子。

translations.literal: Zunshi said, “First ascending to Heaven—he will become Son of Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, “Rising to heaven means he becomes Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 後入于地，不得久也。

translations.literal: “Entering the earth afterward—he will not long remain.”
translations.idiomatic: “Entering the earth means his reign will not last.”

sentences.zh: 」終如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It ended exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 世祖以丞相在京師居守，自致猜疑，甚懷憂懼，謀將起兵，每宿蓍令遵世筮之，遵世云：「不須起動，自有大慶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu as chief minister kept watch in the capital, he brought suspicion on himself and was deeply fearful, planning to raise troops; each night he kept milfoil and had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “There is no need to move; great good fortune will come of itself.”
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, holding the capital as chief minister, feared suspicion and plotted revolt; nightly he had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “Do not move—great fortune will come unbidden.”

sentences.zh: 」俄而趙郡王奉太後令以遺詔追世祖。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Zhao Commandery, acting on the empress dowager’s order and the testamentary edict, summoned Shizu back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Zhao, by the empress dowager’s testament, recalled Shizu.

sentences.zh: 及卽祚，授其中書舍人，固辭疾。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he offered Zunshi the post of Palace Secretariat Draftsman, but Zunshi firmly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he offered Zunshi a secretariat post; Zunshi pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 趙輔和，清都人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fuhe was a native of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fuhe was from Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 少以明《易》善筮為館客。

translations.literal: In youth, because he understood the Changes and was skilled at milfoil divination, he became a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he mastered the Changes and milfoil and served as a house diviner.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩於晉陽，葬有日矣，世宗書令顯祖親卜宅兆相於鄴西北漳水北原。

translations.literal: Gaozu died at Jinyang; the burial day was set, and Shizong wrote ordering Xianzu personally to divine a tomb site and geomantic aspect on the north bank of the Zhang west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu died at Jinyang, Shizong ordered Xianzu to choose a tomb on the Zhang’s north bank west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 顯祖與吳遵世擇地，頻卜不吉，又至一所，命遵世筮之，遇《革》，遵世等數十人咸云不可用。

translations.literal: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi chose ground; repeated divinations were unlucky. At another place he ordered Zunshi to divine and obtained Ge; Zunshi and several dozen others all said it could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi cast repeatedly with ill results; at one site Zunshi drew Ge, and dozens agreed it was unlucky.

sentences.zh: 輔和少年，在衆人之後，進云：「《革卦》於天下人皆凶，唯王家用之大吉。

translations.literal: Fuhe was young and stood behind the crowd; he advanced and said, “The hexagram Ge is ill-omened for all under Heaven, but for a royal house to use it is greatly auspicious.”
translations.idiomatic: Young Fuhe spoke last: “Ge bodes ill for commoners, but for a royal house it is excellent.”

sentences.zh: 《革彖辭》云：『湯武革命，應天順人。

translations.literal: The Judgment of Ge says, “Tang and Wu changed the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people.”
translations.idiomatic: The Ge judgment reads, “Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and the people.”

sentences.zh: 』」顯祖遽登車，顧云：「卽以此地為定。

translations.literal: Xianzu immediately mounted his carriage, turned, and said, “Let this place be fixed.”
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu mounted at once and said, “This is the place.”

sentences.zh: 」卽義平陵也。

translations.literal: This was Yiping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: That became Yiping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 有一人父疾，是人詣館別托相知者筮之，遇《泰》，筮者云：「此卦甚吉，疾愈。

translations.literal: A man’s father was ill; the man went to the lodge and had an acquaintance he entrusted elsewhere divine for him; he obtained Tai, and the diviner said, “This hexagram is very auspicious—the illness will heal.”
translations.idiomatic: When a man’s father fell ill, a friend divined Tai for him and declared the illness would pass.

sentences.zh: 」是人喜。

translations.literal: The man was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The man rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 出後，和謂筮者云：「《泰卦》《乾》下《坤》上，然則入土矣，豈得言吉？

translations.literal: After he left, Fuhe said to the diviner, “In Tai, Qian is below and Kun above—thus one enters the earth; how can you call it auspicious?”
translations.idiomatic: Fuhe told the diviner afterward, “Tai puts Qian under Kun—he goes into the earth; how is that auspicious?”

sentences.zh: 」果以凶問至。

translations.literal: Sure enough news of death arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon came word of death.

sentences.zh: 和大寧、武平中筮後宮誕男女及時日多中，遂授通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the Daning and Wuping eras Fuhe divined for the inner palace on the birth of sons and daughters and the times, and mostly hit true; he was therefore appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In Daning and Wuping he divined palace births and dates with great success and was made regular attendant in direct communication.

sentences.zh: 皇甫玉，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Yu—no one knew from what place he came.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yu’s origins were unknown.

sentences.zh: 善相人，常遊王侯家。

translations.literal: He was skilled at physiognomy and often wandered among princes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomer, he frequented the houses of nobles.

sentences.zh: 世宗自潁川振旅而還，顯祖從後，玉於道旁縱觀，謂人曰：「大將軍不作物，會是道北垂鼻涕者。

translations.literal: When Shizong returned from Yingchuan with his army in array, Xianzu followed behind; Yu watched freely by the roadside and said to someone, “The Grand General will not accomplish the enterprise; it will be the one north of the road who wipes his nose.”
translations.idiomatic: As Shizong marched back from Yingchuan with Xianzu behind, Yu watched from the roadside: “The Grand General will not prevail—the man north of the road who wipes his nose will.”

sentences.zh: 」顯祖旣卽位，試玉相術，故以帛巾袜其眼，而使歷摸諸人。

translations.literal: After Xianzu took the throne he tested Yu’s art, therefore bound his eyes with a cloth kerchief and had him feel his way among the men.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu blindfolded him and had him feel his way among the courtiers to test his art.

sentences.zh: 至於顯祖，曰：「此是最大達官。

translations.literal: Coming to Xianzu, he said, “This is the greatest eminent official.”
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzu he said, “Here is the greatest man in office.”

sentences.zh: 」於任城王，曰：「當至丞相。

translations.literal: Of the Prince of Rencheng he said, “He will reach the chancellorship.”
translations.idiomatic: Of Rencheng he said, “He will reach the chancellorship.”

sentences.zh: 」於常山、長廣二王，並亦貴，而各私掐之。

translations.literal: Of the princes of Changshan and Changuang he also said they would be noble, and privately pinched each of them.
translations.idiomatic: Changshan and Changuang he also called noble—and pinched each in secret.

sentences.zh: 至石動統，曰：「此弄癡人。

translations.literal: Coming to Shi Dongtong, he said, “This is a playing fool.”
translations.idiomatic: At Shi Dongtong he said, “A court fool.”

sentences.zh: 」至供膳，曰：「正得好飲食而已。

translations.literal: Coming to the food server, he said, “He will only get good food and drink.”
translations.idiomatic: At the pantry steward: “Good meals, nothing more.”

sentences.zh: 」玉嘗為高歸彥相，曰：「位極人臣，但莫反。

translations.literal: Yu once read the physiognomy of Gao Guiyan and said, “You will reach the extreme of human rank, only do not rebel.”
translations.idiomatic: Reading Gao Guiyan’s face, Yu said, “You will rise to the summit of rank—only do not rebel.”

sentences.zh: 」歸彥曰：「我何為反？

translations.literal: Guiyan said, “Why would I rebel?”
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan asked, “Why would I rebel?”

sentences.zh: 」玉曰：「不然，公有反骨。

translations.literal: Yu said, “Not so—you have a rebel’s bone.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, “You bear a rebel’s bone.”

sentences.zh: 」玉謂其妻曰：「殿上者不過二年。

translations.literal: Yu told his wife, “The one on the throne will not last two years.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu told his wife, “The throne will not hold two years.”

sentences.zh: 」妻以告舍人斛斯慶，慶以啟帝，帝怒召之。

translations.literal: His wife told the palace attendant Husiqing; Husiqing reported to the emperor, and the emperor angrily summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife told Husiqing, who told the emperor; the emperor summoned him in anger.

sentences.zh: 玉每照鏡，自言當兵死，及被召，謂其妻曰：「我今去不迴，若得過日午時，或當得活。

translations.literal: Yu whenever he looked in the mirror said he was fated to die by weapons; when summoned he told his wife, “I go now and will not return; if I can pass the noon hour, I may yet live.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu had long said he would die by the blade; summoned, he told his wife, “I will not return—unless I pass noon.”

sentences.zh: 」旣至正中，遂斬之。

translations.literal: When the hour reached the center he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At noon he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 世宗時有吳士，雙盲而妙於聲相，世宗歷試之。

translations.literal: In Shizong’s time there was a man of Wu, blind in both eyes yet marvelous in voice physiognomy; Shizong tested him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizong’s day a blind Wu man judged men by voice; Shizong tested him often.

sentences.zh: 聞劉桃枝之聲，曰：「有所繫屬，然當大富貴，王侯將相多死其手，譬如鷹犬為人所使。

translations.literal: Hearing the voice of Liu Taozhi, he said, “He has something he is tied to, yet he will be very rich and noble; many kings, marquises, and chancellors will die by his hand, like hawks and dogs used by men.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taozhi’s voice, he said, betokened great wealth—and many lords would die by his hand, like hawks trained for others.

sentences.zh: 」聞趙道德之聲，曰：「亦繫屬人，富貴翕赫，不及前人。

translations.literal: Hearing the voice of Zhao Daode, he said, “He too is tied to others; his wealth and glory blaze, but not equal to the former.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daode too served others; he would shine, but less than Liu.

sentences.zh: 」聞太原公之聲，曰：「當為人主，」聞世宗之聲，不動，崔暹私掐之，乃謬言：「亦國主也。

translations.literal: Hearing the voice of the Duke of Taiyuan, he said, “He will become a ruler.” Hearing Shizong’s voice he did not stir; Cui Xian privately pinched him, and he then falsely said, “He too is a ruler of a state.”
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan’s voice meant a throne; at Shizong’s he was silent until Cui Xian pinched him, then he lied, “A ruler too.”

sentences.zh: 」世宗以為我群奴猶當極貴，況吾身也。

translations.literal: Shizong thought, “If even my slaves will reach the utmost nobility, how much more my own person.”
translations.idiomatic: Shizong thought, “If my slaves rise so high, what of me?”

sentences.zh: 解法選，河內人。

translations.literal: Jiefa Xuan was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefa Xuan was from Henei.

sentences.zh: 少明相術，鑒照人物，皆如其言。

translations.literal: In youth he understood physiognomy; examining persons in a mirror, all was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: From youth his mirror-reading of faces never failed.

sentences.zh: 頻為和士開相中，士開牒為府參軍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly read He Shikai’s physiognomy favorably; Shikai had him registered as a staff officer in the princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai kept him as mansion staff after repeated favorable readings.

sentences.zh: 魏寧，鉅鹿人。

translations.literal: Wei Ning was a native of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ning was from Julu.

sentences.zh: 以善推祿命征為館客。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled at calculating allotted fate he was summoned as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as house guest for his skill in fate calculation.

sentences.zh: 武成親試之，皆中。

translations.literal: Wucheng personally tested him, and all hit true.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng tested him personally; he never missed.

sentences.zh: 乃以己生年月託為異人而問之，寧曰：「極富貴，今年入墓。

translations.literal: He then gave his own birth year and month, pretending to be another person and asking; Ning said, “Extremely rich and noble—this year he enters the tomb.”
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng disguised his birth date; Ning said, “Supreme fortune—and the tomb this year.”

sentences.zh: 」武成驚曰：「是我！

translations.literal: Wucheng said in alarm, “That is me!”
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng cried, “That is me!”

sentences.zh: 」寧變辭曰：「若帝王，自有法。

translations.literal: Ning changed his words and said, “If an emperor and king, he has his own method.”
translations.idiomatic: Ning backtracked: “Emperors follow other rules.”

sentences.zh: 」又有陽子術，語人曰：「謠言：『盧十六，雉十四，犍子拍頭三十二。

translations.literal: There was also Master Yang’s technique; he told people, “A rhyme says: ‘Lu at sixteen, pheasant at fourteen, the colt beats his head at thirty-two.’”
translations.idiomatic: Master Yang cited a rhyme: “Lu sixteen, pheasant fourteen, the colt strikes his head at thirty-two.”

sentences.zh: 』且四八天之大數，太上之祚，恐不過此。

translations.literal: “Moreover four times eight is Heaven’s great number; the Grand Supreme’s reign, I fear, will not pass this.”
translations.idiomatic: “Four eights are heaven’s great number—the Grand Supreme’s reign will not pass it.”

sentences.zh: 」旣而武成崩，年三十二也。

translations.literal: Before long Wucheng died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng died at thirty-two, as he said.

sentences.zh: 綦母懷文，不知何郡人。

translations.literal: Qimu Huaiwen—no one knew from what commandery he came.
translations.idiomatic: Qimu Huaiwen’s home commandery was unknown.

sentences.zh: 以道術事高祖。

translations.literal: By Daoist arts he served Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Gaozu with Daoist arts.

sentences.zh: 武定初，官軍與周文戰於邙山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, the government army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding the royal army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 是時官軍旗幟盡赤，西軍盡黑，懷文言於高祖曰：「赤火色，黑水色，水能滅火，不宜以赤對黑。

translations.literal: At that time the government army’s banners were all red and the western army all black. Huaiwen said to Gaozu, “Red is the color of fire, black the color of water; water can extinguish fire—red should not face black.”
translations.idiomatic: The royal banners were red, the western army black. Huaiwen said, “Fire against water is ill-omened—do not meet black with red.”

sentences.zh: 土勝水，宜改為黃。

translations.literal: Earth overcomes water; you should change to yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Earth conquers water—use yellow.

sentences.zh: 」高祖遂改為赭黃，所謂河陽幡者。

translations.literal: Gaozu therefore changed to ochre yellow—the so-called Heyang banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu switched to ochre yellow—the Heyang banners.

sentences.zh: 又造宿鐵刀，其法燒生鐵精以重柔鋌，數宿則成剛，以柔鐵為刀脊，浴以五牲之溺，淬以五牲之脂，斬甲過三十札。

translations.literal: He also made night-quenched iron blades: the method is to burn raw iron essence and layer soft ingots; after several nights they become hard; soft iron forms the spine of the blade; it is bathed in the urine of the five sacrificial beasts and quenched in their fat; it can cut through more than thirty layers of armor.
translations.idiomatic: He forged night-quenched blades: layer soft iron on hardened steel, quench in the five beasts’ urine and fat—the edge cut thirty layers of armor.

sentences.zh: 今襄國冶家所鑄宿柔鋌，乃其遺法，作刀猶甚快利，不能截三十札也。

translations.literal: The night-soft ingots that smiths of Xiangguo cast today are his surviving method; blades made from them are still very sharp but cannot cut thirty layers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguo smiths still use his night-soft ingots; their blades are keen but not thirty-fold.

sentences.zh: 懷文云：「廣平郡南斡子城是干將鑄劍處，其土可以瑩刀。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, “South of Guangping Commandery, Ganzi Castle is where Gan Jiang cast swords; its earth can polish blades.”
translations.idiomatic: He said the soil at Ganzi Castle south of Guangping, where Gan Jiang forged swords, polishes blades.

sentences.zh: 」懷文官至信州刺史。

translations.literal: Huaiwen rose to Inspector of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen became inspector of Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 又有孫正言，謂人曰：「我昔武定中為廣州士曹，聞城人曹普演言：『高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之，當滅。

translations.literal: There was also Sun Zhengyan, who told people, “In Wuding I was a clerical officer in Guang Province and heard the townsman Cao Puyan say, ‘Among Prince Gao’s sons, Abao will become Son of Heaven; when it reaches Degao’s Chengzhi, there will be destruction.’”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhengyan recalled hearing in Guangzhou during Wuding: “Among Gao’s sons, Abao will reign; when Degao’s Chengzhi comes, the line ends.”

sentences.zh: 』」阿保謂天保，德之謂德昌也，滅年號承光，卽承之也。

translations.literal: Abao means Tianbao, Degao means Dechang; the destroyed reign title Chengguang is precisely Chengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Abao is Tianbao, Degao is Dechang; the doomed era Chengguang is Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 張子信，河內人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zixin was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zixin was from Henei.

sentences.zh: 性清凈，頗涉文學。

translations.literal: By nature pure and quiet, he was fairly versed in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and literate by nature.

sentences.zh: 少以醫術知名，恒隱於白鹿山。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for medical skill and constantly hid on White Deer Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Famed young as a physician, he lived as a hermit on White Deer Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時遊京邑，甚為魏收、崔季舒等所禮，有贈答子信詩數篇。

translations.literal: He sometimes traveled to the capital and was greatly honored by Wei Shou, Cui Jishu, and others; there are several poems exchanged with Zixin.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Wei Shou and Cui Jishu honored him; poems between them survive.

sentences.zh: 後魏以太中大夫徵之，聽其時還山，不常在鄴。

translations.literal: Later Wei appointed him Grand Master of Palace Leisure and allowed him to return to the mountains at times; he was not constantly at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him grand master of palace leisure, letting him return to the hills; he was seldom at Ye.

sentences.zh: 又善易卜風角。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in Changes divination and wind angles.
translations.idiomatic: He also read the Changes and the winds.

sentences.zh: 武衛奚永洛與子信對坐，有鵲鳴於庭樹，鬥而墮焉。

translations.literal: Guard of Martial Valor Xi Yongluo sat facing Zixin; a magpie cried in the courtyard tree, fought, and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yongluo sat with Zixin when magpies fought in the courtyard tree and fell.

sentences.zh: 子信曰：「鵲言不善，向夕若有風從西南來，歷此樹，拂堂角，則有口舌事。

translations.literal: Zixin said, “The magpie’s speech is unlucky; toward evening if wind comes from the southwest, passes this tree, and brushes the hall corner, there will be a matter of quarrel.”
translations.idiomatic: Zixin said, “The magpie foretells trouble; if southwest wind brushes this tree and the hall corner at dusk, quarrels follow.”

sentences.zh: 今夜有人喚，必不得往，雖敕，亦以病辭。

translations.literal: “Tonight if someone summons you, you must not go; even if it is an edict, plead illness.”
translations.idiomatic: “If summoned tonight, refuse—even an edict; plead illness.”

sentences.zh: 」子信去後，果有風如其言。

translations.literal: After Zixin left, wind came indeed as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Wind came as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 是夜，琅邪王五使切召永洛，且雲敕喚。

translations.literal: That night the fifth son of the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, saying it was an edict summons.
translations.idiomatic: That night Langye’s fifth son urgently summoned Yongluo, claiming an edict.

sentences.zh: 永洛欲起，其妻苦留之，稱墜馬腰折。

translations.literal: Yongluo was about to rise; his wife forcibly detained him, saying he had fallen from a horse and broken his waist.
translations.idiomatic: His wife held him back, claiming a fall had broken his waist.

sentences.zh: 詰朝而難作。

translations.literal: At dawn the calamity broke out.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the coup erupted.

sentences.zh: 子信齊亡卒。

translations.literal: Zixin died when Qi perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zixin died with the fall of Qi.

sentences.zh: 馬嗣明，河內人。

translations.literal: Ma Siming was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Siming was from Henei.

sentences.zh: 少明醫術，博綜經方，《甲乙》、《素問》、《明堂》、《本草》莫不咸誦。

translations.literal: In youth he understood medical arts and broadly mastered classical prescriptions; the Jade A, Plain Questions, Bright Hall, and Root Canon of Materia Medica—none did he not recite.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered medicine and the classics—Jade A, Plain Questions, Bright Hall, and the materia medica canon.

sentences.zh: 為人診候，一年前知其生死。

translations.literal: When diagnosing people, he knew their life or death a year in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He could tell life or death a year ahead.

sentences.zh: 邢卲子大寶患傷寒，嗣明為之診，候脉，退告楊愔云：「邢公子傷寒不治自差，然脈候不出一年便死，覺之晚，不可治。

translations.literal: Xing Shao’s son Dabao had cold damage; Siming examined him and felt his pulse, then withdrew and told Yang Yin, “Young master Xing’s cold damage will heal without treatment, yet the pulse shows he will die within a year; noticed too late, it cannot be cured.”
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Shao’s son Dabao fell ill, Siming said to Yang Yin, “The cold will pass, but the pulse shows death within a year—too late to cure.”

sentences.zh: 」楊、邢並侍宴內殿，顯祖云：「子才兒，我欲乞其隨近一郡。

translations.literal: Yang and Xing both attended a banquet in the inner hall; Xianzu said, “Zicai’s son—I wish to beg a nearby commandery for him.”
translations.idiomatic: At court Xianzu said he would give Dabao a nearby commandery.

sentences.zh: 」楊以此子年少，未合剖符，讌罷，奏云：「馬嗣明稱大寶脉惡，一年內恐死，若其出郡，醫藥難求。

translations.literal: Yang, because the son was young and not yet fit to receive a seal, after the feast memorialized, “Ma Siming says Dabao’s pulse is ill and he may die within a year; if he goes to a commandery, medicine will be hard to obtain.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang objected after the feast: “Siming says Dabao’s pulse is fatal within a year—a distant post leaves him without care.”

sentences.zh: 」遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was therefore dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 大寶未期而卒。

translations.literal: Dabao died before the year was out.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao died within the year.

sentences.zh: 楊令患背腫，嗣明以練石塗之便差。

translations.literal: When Magistrate Yang had a swelling on his back, Siming smeared refined stone on it and it healed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Siming cured Yang’s back abscess with refined stone paste.

sentences.zh: 作練石法：以粗黃色石鵝鴨卵大，猛火燒令赤，內淳醋中，自屑，頻燒至石盡，取石屑曝乾，搗下簁。

translations.literal: The method for making refined stone: take coarse yellow stone the size of a goose or duck egg, burn it fiercely until red, place it in pure vinegar until it crumbles, burn repeatedly until the stone is gone, take the crumbs, dry them in the sun, pound and sift.
translations.idiomatic: Refined stone: heat yellow cobbles to red, quench in vinegar until they crumble, dry and sift the powder.

sentences.zh: 和醋以塗腫上，無不愈。

translations.literal: Mix with vinegar and smear on the swelling—none fail to heal.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed with vinegar and applied, no swelling failed to heal.

sentences.zh: 後遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Regular Attendant in Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He later became regular attendant in direct communication.

sentences.zh: 針灸孔穴，往往與《明堂》不同。

translations.literal: The acupoints for needling and cautery often differed from the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His acupuncture points often differed from the Bright Hall canon.

sentences.zh: 從駕往晉陽，至遼陽山中，數處見牓，云有人家女病，若有能治差者，購錢十萬。

translations.literal: Following the imperial progress to Jinyang, in the mountains of Liaoyang he saw placards in several places saying a family’s daughter was ill and that whoever could cure her would receive a reward of a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Jinyang in Liaoyang hills, placards offered a hundred thousand cash to heal a girl.

sentences.zh: 諸名醫多尋牓至，問病狀，不敢下手。

translations.literal: Many famous physicians sought out the placards and came, asked the symptoms, and dared not treat.
translations.idiomatic: Famous doctors came, read the case, and dared not treat.

sentences.zh: 唯嗣明獨治之。

translations.literal: Only Siming alone treated her.
translations.idiomatic: Only Siming took the case.

sentences.zh: 問其病由。

translations.literal: He asked the origin of the illness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked how the illness began.

sentences.zh: 云曾以手將一麥穟，卽見一赤物長二寸，似蛇，入其手指中，因驚怖倒地，卽覺手臂疼腫，漸及半身俱腫，痛不可忍，呻吟晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: She said she had once held an ear of wheat in her hand and at once saw a red thing two inches long, like a snake, enter her finger; startled and terrified she fell to the ground, and at once felt pain and swelling in her arm, gradually reaching the whole half of her body, with pain unbearable and groaning day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: She had touched a wheat ear; a red serpent-like thing two inches long entered her finger. Her arm swelled to half her body in agony day and night.

sentences.zh: 嗣明為處方服湯。

translations.literal: Siming prescribed a decoction for her to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Siming gave her a decoction.

sentences.zh: 比嗣明從駕還，女平復。

translations.literal: By the time Siming returned from following the imperial progress, the girl had recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from court, she was healed.

sentences.zh: 嗣明，隋初卒。

translations.literal: Siming died in the early Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Siming died in early Sui.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Book Company in November 1972.
translations.idiomatic: This text has been collated against the Zhonghua Book Company first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
